company.name: Quality Power Electrical Equipments Ltd
company.about: Quality Power makes high-voltage grid equipment: air-core reactors, line traps, instrument transformers, STATCOM/SVC systems and power-conversion systems for battery storage, used in HVDC, FACTS and transmission projects. Roughly three-quarters of revenue comes from exports to utilities and grid OEMs in Europe, the Middle East, the Americas and Japan. It manufactures in Sangli (Maharashtra), Kerala and Türkiye, where its 51%-owned subsidiary Endoks is based.

events.title: Stock falls 6.35% to ₹1,305, down 10% on the week and 10.6% below the ₹1,460 Winwin swap price
events.details: Quality Power shares closed at ₹1,305.25 on 23 October, down 6.35% on the day and about 10% for the week, the fourth straight decline since the 19 October EGM on the Winwin Insulators share swap and ₹700 crore QIP. The price is now roughly 10.6% below the ₹1,460 per share swap price and well under the early-October record near ₹1,680. No company announcement explained it. The fall coincided with a sell-off in US AI-power names such as GE Vernova and weak Indian capital-goods shares. The scrutinizer's report on the EGM vote has been listed but vote counts were not read.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a lower share price means a ₹700 crore QIP would need more new shares, and the Winwin sellers are receiving shares now worth less than the ₹1,460 agreed.

events.title: New Global Coil Factory at Sangli starts commercial production of HV air-core reactors
events.details: Quality Power said its greenfield Global Coil Factory at Kupwad MIDC, Sangli, began commercial manufacturing on 20 October 2026. The plant makes high-voltage air-core dry-type reactors and coil products for HVAC, HVDC, FACTS and renewable grid-connection projects, and has coil-winding lines, a high-voltage test lab and conductor processing. Output will ramp up in phases. The disclosure gave no capacity, capex or revenue figure. At the June 2025 groundbreaking the company had described it as one of the world's largest reactor plants, with 44 winding lines.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: coils are among the group's highest-margin products, so a large domestic plant could shift the mix away from the 51%-owned Turkish subsidiary, but the benefit depends on how fast customers qualify the plant.

events.title: EGM held on Winwin share swap and ₹700 Cr QIP; voting results not yet published
events.details: The company held its first extraordinary general meeting since listing on 19 October 2026 by video conference. Shareholders voted on special resolutions to issue shares to selling shareholders of Winwin Speciality Insulators as part of the acquisition price, and to raise up to ₹700 crore through a qualified institutional placement. The outcome filing records the proceedings and attendance but, as indexed, not the vote counts. Promoters hold about 73.9%, so approval was widely expected. The stock fell 3.25% to ₹1,407.10 that day, below the ₹1,460 swap price.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: approval would clear the way for the Winwin closing and the QIP, which together bring roughly 6–7% dilution at current prices.

events.title: Turkish subsidiary Endoks starts production at new PCS/BESS converter plant in Niğde
events.details: Endoks Energy Systems, the 51%-owned Turkish subsidiary, began manufacturing at its new plant in Niğde, Türkiye, which makes power-conversion systems (PCS) for battery energy storage. The company disclosed the start in a Regulation 30 filing on 17 October 2026. Management had guided for the plant in the third quarter of FY27, so it came in on time or slightly early. No capacity, capex or revenue estimate was given. The BESS/PCS line is a key growth area: management targeted US$60–80 million of such orders in FY27.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: extra PCS capacity supports the battery-storage order pipeline, though 49% of Endoks' profit goes to minority holders.

events.title: Stock falls 5.1% to ₹1,433.80, slipping below the ₹1,460 Winwin swap price before the EGM
events.details: Shares fell about 5.1% to around ₹1,433.80, touching an intraday low of ₹1,411.20, with no company announcement behind the move. That took the price below the ₹1,460 at which shares are to be issued to Winwin's sellers and the ₹1,456.40 regulatory floor price. The slide continued into the 19 October EGM, when the stock closed at ₹1,407.10; it was down about 7% for the week and about 16% below its 6 October all-time high.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: weakness before a ₹700 crore QIP matters because a lower placement price means more new shares for the same money.

events.title: Stock hits an all-time high near ₹1,680, about 4x its ₹425 IPO price
events.details: Quality Power shares made a run of record highs from late September and peaked on 6 October 2026, with aggregators putting the 52-week high at about ₹1,680–1,681. At about ₹1,649 the market value was roughly ₹12,770 crore and the trailing P/E about 65 times consolidated earnings. The stock then eased back to around ₹1,524 by 12 October as attention turned to the equity issuance tied to the Winwin deal and the planned QIP.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the rally priced in a lot of execution, which is why later dilution and margin news moved the stock sharply.

events.title: 25th AGM approves FY26 final dividend of ₹1 per share
events.details: Shareholders at the 25th annual general meeting, held by video conference on 29 September 2026, approved a final dividend of ₹1 per share for FY26, payable by 28 October. Together with the ₹0.25 interim dividend declared with the Q1 FY27 results, the payout is small relative to the share price, a yield below 0.1%. The FY26 annual report and AGM notice had been filed on 5 September.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the token payout signals the company is keeping cash for capacity and acquisitions.

events.title: Board approves Winwin Speciality Insulators buy for up to ₹272 Cr and a QIP of up to ₹700 Cr
events.details: The board approved buying up to 100% of Winwin Speciality Insulators for up to ₹272.34 crore and signed the share purchase agreement. Of that, ₹123.84 crore is cash and the rest is 10,17,123 new Quality Power shares at ₹1,460 each. Winwin makes ceramic insulators, an input the company has called a supply bottleneck; its FY26 revenue was about ₹17 crore, so the price is roughly 16 times sales. The board also approved raising up to ₹700 crore through a qualified institutional placement, and called an EGM for 19 October.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: backward integration eases a supply constraint, but the rich price and the QIP mean dilution for existing holders.

events.title: POWERGRID awards 6,000 MW Barmer–South Kalamb HVDC link to GE Vernova T&D, a key customer
events.details: POWERGRID, which won the ±800 kV Barmer-II to South Kalamb HVDC transmission project (about ₹3,244 crore, letter of intent 2 September), awarded the HVDC package to GE Vernova T&D India in early September 2026. The link will carry 6,000 MW of renewable power from Rajasthan. Separately, the Cabinet approved Green Energy Corridor Phase III. Quality Power supplies reactors and coils for HVDC projects and counts GE Vernova among its customers, though no Quality Power order from this project has been disclosed.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: more domestic HVDC awards widen the market for Quality Power's reactors, but any direct order still has to be announced.

events.title: Board defers Winwin preferential issue; recommends CMD Thalavaidurai Pandyan's re-appointment
events.details: At its 2 September 2026 meeting the board put off a proposed preferential issue of shares and warrants to Winwin's shareholders, citing further evaluation of fund-raising options and ongoing due diligence. It also recommended re-appointing promoter Thalavaidurai Pandyan as Chairman and Managing Director for five years from 1 March 2027, subject to shareholder approval. Three weeks later the board revived the share-swap in a revised form alongside the QIP proposal.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the back-and-forth on deal terms is worth tracking as a governance signal; leadership continuity is unchanged.

events.title: Stock hits 5% upper circuit at ₹1,178.40 as Q1 call reiterates 15–20% FY27 growth
events.details: A day after the Q1 FY27 results, the shares rose 5% to the upper circuit at ₹1,178.40. On the earnings call management kept its FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15–20%, calling FY27 a stabilisation year before faster growth in FY28 as new capacity comes on. Priorities named were commissioning and qualifying the Sangli coil plant, adding PCS/BESS capacity in Türkiye and closing the Winwin acquisition. No explicit margin or capex guidance was given.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: Q1 growth of 32% was already ahead of the full-year guide, which the market read as room for upgrades.

events.title: Q1 FY27: income up 32% to ₹256 Cr, adjusted PAT up 47% to ₹54.5 Cr; order book ₹1,945 Cr
events.details: For the June 2026 quarter, consolidated total income rose 32% year on year to ₹256.4 crore. Reported profit after tax was ₹46.7 crore; excluding a ₹7.8 crore non-cash hyperinflation accounting loss at the Turkish subsidiary, adjusted PAT was ₹54.5 crore, up 46.9%. The order book reached ₹1,945.5 crore, about 1.9 times FY26 revenue. The board declared an interim dividend of ₹0.25, took on record due diligence on Winwin with no adverse findings, and appointed Bathiya Advisors as internal auditor.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the larger order book gives revenue visibility into FY28, though the adjusted figure strips out a recurring Turkish accounting charge.

events.title: Endoks wins ₹40.9 Cr FACTS order in Japan; Mehru wins ₹15.7 Cr orders from Hitachi Energy
events.details: In early July 2026 the group reported two orders. Endoks, the Turkish subsidiary, won a high-voltage FACTS contract in Japan worth about ₹40.9 crore, to be executed by December 2027. Mehru, the 51%-owned instrument-transformer subsidiary, won orders worth ₹15.70 crore from Hitachi Energy India for 400 kV instrument transformers. With the US data-centre reactor order, these made up most of the ₹104.9 crore of disclosed order wins in the quarter.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the orders broaden the customer base into Japan and deepen ties with a major grid OEM, though each is small relative to revenue.

events.title: Q4 call: management guides 15–20% revenue growth for FY27 and US$60–80 Mn of BESS/PCS orders
events.details: On the Q4 FY26 earnings call, management guided for 15–20% revenue growth in FY27, a sharp slowdown after FY26's near-tripling of revenue, which included newly consolidated businesses. It set a target of US$60–80 million of battery-storage power-conversion orders for the year. Management flagged risks from metal-price inflation, geopolitics, shortages of insulators and winding conductors, and container logistics. FY26 guidance of more than ₹900 crore revenue and more than 22% EBITDA margin had been met.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the guide reset growth expectations lower and showed that input costs and supply bottlenecks are the main margin risks.

events.title: FY26: revenue up 180% to ₹947 Cr, PAT up 85% to ₹185.5 Cr; order book above ₹1,400 Cr
events.details: Consolidated revenue from operations for FY26 rose about 180% to ₹947 crore and total income passed ₹1,000 crore, helped by the first full year of the Mehru acquisition. Profit after tax rose 85% to ₹185.5 crore. In the March quarter, total income was ₹309.8 crore and PAT ₹50.6 crore, up 66%, but EBITDA margin fell to about 19% because of a ₹25.7 crore hyperinflation accounting loss in Türkiye and one-time labour-code provisions. The order book exceeded ₹1,400 crore. The board recommended a final dividend of ₹1.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: growth was strong, but full-year EBITDA margin fell to about 23.5% from about 30.5%, and Turkish accounting charges keep recurring.

events.title: Wins ₹48.3 Cr high-voltage reactor order for a US data-centre project
events.details: Quality Power received an order worth about ₹48.3 crore, excluding taxes, to supply high-voltage reactors for a data-centre project in the United States, to be executed within about 12 months. The customer was not named because of a non-disclosure agreement. It was the largest single order disclosed in the June 2026 quarter and the company's first notable win tied to data-centre power demand.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: data centres are a new demand source beyond utilities, though US tariff policy is a risk for such exports.

events.title: Postal ballot re-appoints Rajendra Sheshadri Iyer as independent director with 99.99% approval
events.details: Shareholders approved, by postal ballot, a second term for Rajendra Sheshadri Iyer as an independent director. E-voting ran from 14 March to 12 April 2026 and the results were filed on 14 April. A secondary report puts approval at 99.9987% of votes cast, with about 6.18 crore of 7.74 crore shares voting. It was the only resolution on the ballot.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: routine board continuity; no change to the governance picture.

events.title: Endoks wins ₹152 Cr battery storage order, expandable to ₹292 Cr
events.details: The Turkish subsidiary Endoks won an order to design, make and supply battery energy storage systems of 50 MW/55 MWh and 40 MW/80 MWh, worth about ₹152 crore with potential to rise to ₹292 crore. Execution is targeted by December 2027. The customer was not disclosed under confidentiality terms, and the company said no promoter or group entity has an interest in the awarding party. The base value is about 16% of FY26 revenue.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the largest single order disclosed so far, and evidence that the battery-storage line can win sizeable contracts.

events.title: Q3 FY26: income up 257% to record ₹284 Cr, PAT up 221% to ₹62.8 Cr; Sangli plant pulled forward
events.details: For the December 2025 quarter, total income rose 256.5% year on year to a record ₹284.3 crore and EBITDA reached ₹79.3 crore, a 27.9% margin. Profit after tax rose about 221% to ₹62.8 crore, with earnings per share of ₹5.03. The company said the Sangli coil plant's completion had been brought forward to June 2026, that an expansion in Cochin was complete, and that the 50% acquisition of Sukrut Electric, held jointly with Yash Highvoltage, had closed.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the best quarter to date on both revenue and margin, which underpinned the stock's later re-rating.

events.details: For the September 2025 quarter, consolidated revenue rose 112% year on year to ₹218.9 crore, EBITDA rose 193% to ₹49.4 crore and profit after tax rose 162% to ₹35.2 crore. The order book stood at about ₹830 crore. Management credited execution on HVDC and FACTS projects, including smoothing reactors for the Rihand–Dadri HVDC link supplied with Hitachi Energy India. The Mehru acquisition added to the year-on-year growth.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the first quarter in which the scale-up after listing showed clearly in both revenue and profit.

events.title: Wins ₹34.75 Cr shunt reactor order from Abu Dhabi Transmission Company
events.details: Quality Power won an order worth about ₹34.75 crore from Abu Dhabi Transmission Company, a UAE utility, for dry-type and oil-filled shunt reactors built with its Dry-Q technology. The equipment is to be made at Sangli and delivered over about a year. The company said it won against European and Chinese competitors. The shares rose on the order and the Q1 results announced the previous day.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a direct utility win in the Gulf against global rivals supports the export-led growth case.

events.title: Q1 FY26: record revenue of ₹194 Cr, more than double a year ago; PAT ₹37.1 Cr; backlog ₹775 Cr
events.details: For the June 2025 quarter, total revenue more than doubled year on year to a record ₹194.1 crore and profit after tax rose about 11% to ₹37.1 crore. The order backlog stood above ₹775 crore. During the quarter the company won, with Hitachi Energy India, an order for 500 kV smoothing reactors for POWERGRID's ±500 kV Rihand–Dadri HVDC link; its value was not disclosed. Profit grew much more slowly than revenue: Capital Market put EBITDA margin at 17.5%, against 38.4% a year earlier.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: revenue scale-up was strong, but the gap between revenue and profit growth flagged the margin dilution from acquisitions.

events.title: Term sheet to buy Sukrut Electric with Yash Highvoltage; stock jumps 15% to a record ₹822.90
events.details: Quality Power and Yash Highvoltage signed a binding term sheet to buy 100% of Sukrut Electric, a Pune-based maker of transformer components, from a German multinational. The shares rose as much as 14.97% to a then record ₹822.90 and closed up 12.2% at ₹803. The deal was later restructured: in October 2025 the company agreed to buy 50% for €5 lakh (about ₹5.2 crore), with Yash Highvoltage holding the other half, and the acquisition closed by February 2026.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a small deal by value; the share reaction mattered more than the business added.

events.title: Breaks ground on Global Coil Factory at Sangli, planned with 44 winding lines
events.details: Quality Power held the groundbreaking for its Global Coil Factory at Kupwad MIDC, Sangli. The plant is planned as one of the world's largest for air-core and oil-filled reactors, with 44 winding lines and a high-voltage test lab, built to IGBC Platinum green-building standards. The board had approved the capex on 27 May 2025. One report put the cost above ₹700 crore with operations by December 2026; the company did not confirm that figure in the sources found.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the main capacity bet after the IPO, aimed at the global HVDC and FACTS reactor market.

events.title: FY25: total revenue ₹392 Cr, PAT up 80% to ₹100 Cr; Q4 PAT up 74% to ₹30.5 Cr
events.details: In its first annual results as a listed company, Quality Power reported FY25 consolidated total revenue of ₹392.3 crore and profit after tax of ₹100.1 crore, up about 80%. For the March 2025 quarter, total revenue was ₹129.9 crore and PAT rose 74.1% to ₹30.5 crore, a 23.5% margin. At the same meeting the board approved capital spending on the new Sangli coil factory. Some auto-generated reports carried lower figures, apparently on a different basis.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a clean first year after listing, with EBITDA margins near 30% that later diluted as acquisitions were consolidated.

events.title: Buys 51% of instrument-transformer maker Mehru Electrical for ₹120 Cr; shares jump ~11%
events.details: Two weeks after listing, Quality Power agreed to buy 51% of Mehru Electrical & Mechanical Engineers for ₹120 crore in cash. Mehru makes high-voltage instrument transformers for utilities, industry and transmission networks and adds products rated up to 500 kV. The company said the deal would broaden its technology, manufacturing scale and market reach. The shares rose about 10.7% intraday on 7 March 2025.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: Mehru was the main driver of the jump in consolidated revenue in FY26, but at lower margins than the core reactor business.

events.title: Lists on NSE and BSE after ₹859 Cr IPO priced at ₹425 per share
events.details: Quality Power's shares began trading on 24 February 2025 after an initial public offering that ran from 14 to 18 February. The issue, priced at the top of the ₹401–425 band, raised about ₹858.7 crore: a fresh issue of about ₹225 crore and an offer for sale of about ₹633.7 crore. One tracker reports a listing price of ₹430, a gain of about 1%; that figure was not confirmed elsewhere. Promoters held about 73.9% after the issue.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: most of the IPO was a promoter sale, so the company itself raised only about ₹225 crore for growth.
